scenarios.context: Two classmates talk about their exam preparation.

speakerA.en: I'm going to hit the books tonight. The exam is on Monday.
Do you have to learn the vocabulary by heart?
Don't push yourself too hard. Sleep matters, too.
Good. In the long run, rest helps you remember more.

speakerB.en: Me too. I'll probably burn the midnight oil.
Yes, all fifty words. It's a lot, but I want to pass with flying colours.
You're right. I'll call it a day at eleven.
True. See you after the exam, and good luck!

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about a coding class.

speakerA.en: How's your new coding class going?
That's great! I tried it once, and I was back to square one after every mistake.
Do you do anything special to improve?
Smart. Maybe I should try again.

speakerB.en: Slowly. It's hard, but I'm starting to get the hang of it.
Me too, at the beginning. Now I make fewer mistakes.
I kill two birds with one stone: I practise English while I read the tutorials.
Do it! The ball is in your court, and I'm happy to help.

scenarios.context: A son asks his father to buy expensive sneakers.

speakerA.en: Dad, can I have the new sneakers? They're the latest model.
A hundred and twenty dollars. All my friends have them.
I know, but I would take care of them.
That's fair. I'll start saving for them today.

speakerB.en: How much are they?
That costs a fortune! Money doesn't grow on trees, you know.
Why don't we make a deal? I'll pay half, and you save the rest from your pocket money.
Good. And remember to save for a rainy day, too.

scenarios.context: A girl is disappointed about a school play.

speakerA.en: I didn't get the part in the school play. I was so disappointed.
How could that be? I practised for weeks.
Hmm, that's true. I hadn't thought of it that way.
You always know what to say. Thanks for cheering me up.

speakerB.en: I'm sorry. But maybe it's a blessing in disguise.
Now you'll have time for the art contest, and you're great at painting.
Everything happens for a reason, as my grandma says.
Anytime. Let's go and look at the contest rules together.

scenarios.context: A student has joined too many clubs.

speakerA.en: I joined three clubs, and now I have no free time at all.
I think so. I'm exhausted, and my marks are dropping.
Definitely chess. The other two are just okay.
You're right. I'll tell my teachers tomorrow.

speakerB.en: It sounds like you bit off more than you can chew.
Which club do you enjoy the most?
Then keep chess and leave the others. It will take a weight off your shoulders.
Good. It's better to do a few things well than many things badly.
